newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees NZ GDP growth of 2 pct in yr to Mar 98.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees NZ GDP growth of 2 pct in yr to Mar 98.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand in its six monthly Monetary Policy Statement on Friday projected real annual average economic growth would be 2.0 percent in the year to March 1998.
It projects annual average growth of 3.6 percent in the year to March 1999 and 3.8 percent the following year.
The bank's projections compare with Treasury's growth projections published in the budget on Thursday of 2.4 percent in 1998, 4.2 percent in 1999 and 3.5 percent in 2000.
Statistics New Zealand said seasonally adjusted annual average GDP grew 2.9 percent in 1996.
The RBNZ said it now believed the economy grew more slowly in the first two quarters of 1997 than it thought likely when it when it issued its March Economic Projections.

"Indicators for the March quarter in particular suggest that there was quite an abrupt slowing during the first three months of the year. Indeed, it is not inconceivable that the economy may even have contracted slightly in that quarter," Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said.

"Indicators for the June quarter, however, together with our own business contacts, suggest that the economy may have rebounded somewhat in that quarter, and we currently project that growth will strengthen in subsequent quarters."
The RBNZ projected quarterly GDP growth of 0.3 percent in the June 1997 quarter followed by 0.4 percent, 0.7 percent and 0.9 percent in succeeding quarters.
